title: Use a process explainer to show the steps of a public process and who acts at each one.
rule: Give each level of government, and the public where it acts, a column named in words at its head, and set each step in a box across the columns of those who act at it, numbered in the order the law sets and joined by arrows in the text’s ink. A step some cases take in place of another sits under it with a gray edge and a line that says when it applies; steps that follow one step side by side share a row, each with its own arrow. Print each time as the law’s limit, never as a wait, and the date of the law once, in the grade line. Name every actor in words, since no symbol means a governor, an agency or the President, and give the table every step in reading order with where it leads. On a phone the steps run down one column, each naming who acts.
use_when: The reader asks how a public process runs across levels of government and who has to ask or act at each step, such as how a disaster declaration brings federal help.

use_instead.when: One institution’s steps, with where others can step in
The steps a reader takes, in order
How long each step can take for one person

text: A column for each level lets a reader find where their own government acts by reading down one column, and the numbered path keeps the order when the drawing is read aloud or as a table. Naming each actor in words keeps a symbol from taking a meaning it was never given.
why.basis: Design judgment, from the chart system our founder and editor approved in November 2026

builders: Form process-explainer: node work/build/chart-kit/oa-chart.mjs build s89; encode key, path, step, level, who and limit; labels.lanes names each column and the levels it holds, labels.branches gives a step taken in place of another (at), labels.together sets steps side by side in one row, and labels.limit_words prints each limit in its words.
